rationale: The build job has no explicit timeout, so a hung or runaway job can consume the default 360-minute runner budget. Evidence pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout) supports adding an explicit job budget to reduce runaway consumption, with reported VM-time reduction for free runners. The change is minimal: add timeout-minutes: 60 to the build job. All build/test steps, the matrix (g++/clang++ over glibc), fail-fast: false, path filters, and concurrency cancellation are preserved, so intended coverage and required-check semantics are unchanged. Historical CI runs show successful completions well under this bound (the slowest success is about 15 minutes), giving operational headroom for cold dependency installation without risking false timeouts on valid runs. No new network access, secrets, privileged actions, publishing, or deployment operations are introduced.
